- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply 2–3 day lag correction: use 7-day average of true values as baseline for next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 14-day moving average of past 30d true values.
